facts.fact: Google claims that AdWords location extensions can boost clickthrough rate by up to 10%.
facts.quote: Google claims that AdWords location extensions can **boost clickthrough rate by up to 10%**.

facts.fact: As of 2014, location extension info is based on the linked Google My Business account, and it is no longer possible to manually upload business listings to AdWords.
facts.quote: As of 2014, your location extension info is based on your linked [Google My Business](https://www.google.com/business/) account.

facts.fact: Advertisers are charged the same CPC for whichever location extension action the user takes, whether visiting the website, clicking through to maps, or calling.
facts.quote: You’ll be charged the same CPC for whichever action the user takes, whether she visits your website, clicks through to maps, or calls you.

facts.fact: Mobile clicks-to-call and Get direction clicks from location extensions are not tracked through to conversions, according to the blog.
facts.quote: Note that Mobile clicks-to-call and Get direction are not tracked through to conversions

facts.fact: Phone numbers used from location extensions do not have a forwarding number, so click-to-call measures initiated calls but not the rich call data available from call extensions.
facts.quote: Remember that phone numbers used from location extensions don’t have a forwarding number.

facts.fact: After linking accounts, the blog says location extensions should be running within 24 hours.
facts.quote: Your location extensions should be running within 24 hours!

facts.fact: The Google My Business and AdWords accounts need to share the same email address for the linking process.
facts.quote: Your Google My Business and AdWords account need to have the same email address
